newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks seen nearing dip but tone firm.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks seen nearing dip but tone firm.

text.p: A steady rise in Hong Kong's Hang Seng index is bringing the blue chip barometer closer to a correction but analysts said market momentum could limit any fall in the week ahead.
"I think the market still wants to take a breather but it still has momentum to it," said Geoff Galbraith, institutional sales trader at Nava SC Securities.
The Hang Seng index gained 227.42 points, or 1.76 percent, last week to close at 13,116.79 points on Friday, up 17.23 points on the day. The index is up 5.12 percent this month.
Analysts said a re-rating of property investment companies, following the sale of the Entertainment Building in Hong Kong's Central district for a bumper price, could give the market further impetus.
Chinese Estates Holdings Ltd said last week it had agreed to sell the commercial and office block to Hysan Development Ltd for HK$3.64 billion (US$471 million).
"The index can still keep momentum because of a re-rating of certain property investors," said Kelvin Tang, analyst at ImPac Asset Management.

He expected the Hang Seng index to remain around 13,000 points. "It still depends on the U.S. market. If the re-rating of the property stocks continues the market can still trend upwards. Otherwise I see a mild correction down to 12,800."
Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities, expected a range of 12,800 to 13,300 in the week ahead.

"I am a little bit cautious at this level, particularly as the market still lacks a meaningful correction. The risk of a correction is increasing. Profit-taking pressures are increasing at higher levels," he said.

Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities, said the trading range could be wide if the market begins to correct. "Once the correction starts the market could start falling," he said, predicting a range of 12,900 to 13,400.

"The market has been in need of a correction for some time but it just hasn't started it yet. The buyers don't think it is time yet and they are not quite ready to let the sellers come out in strength," he said.
Two new issues, Jackin International Holdings Ltd and Citybus Group Ltd, are due to begin trading.

Jackin, a magnetic data storage products manufacturer, offered 90.75 million shares at HK$1.05 per share. The offering was expected to be 250 times subscribed, market sources said, and trading in the shares is due to begin on November 28.

Bus operator Citybus, a unit of CNT Group Ltd, offered 250 million shares at HK$1.42 per share, of which 166 million shares were offered to the public. The initial public offering was 18.2 times subscribed and trading in the shares is due to begin on November 29.

Hopewell Holdings Ltd and its Consolidated Electric Power Asia Ltd (CEPA) unit are due to hold special shareholder meetings on Monday following a deal last month in which Hopewell agreed to sell a major part of its CEPA stake to Southern Electric International Inc.
Amoy Properties Ltd and Hang Lung Development Co Ltd are scheduled to hold their annual general meetings on Tuesday.
